conventions.convention: Under Countable Choice, windows are bounded Borel sets of positive finite Lebesgue measure, their volumes diverge, and every compact Minkowski enlargement has measurable excess of negligible relative volume.

Spatial integration requires joint Borel-product measurability. The window average is defined by the sample-path integral where absolutely integrable and is zero on the measurable exceptional null set.

Only positive pair counts are admissible. The covariance estimator is the pair-count average of raw products minus the square of the global sample mean; the semivariogram divides the sum of squared increments by twice the pair count.
The lattice character associated with a circle tuple z is k ↦ product z_r raised to k_r; angular coordinates give the positive-exponent character exp(i k·θ).

The known-mean periodogram uses the negative Fourier exponent and normalization 1/((2π)^d n^d). Torus integration uses unnormalized product angular Lebesgue measure. Smoothing uses nonnegative normalized Fourier-grid weights and is undefined when their denominator vanishes.

The continuous-space spectral representation has no Fourier prefactor. At spacing δ, the angular density is δ^(-d) times the sum of translated continuous-space densities; a specified Borel representative determines this pointwise sum.

Bias limits require a bounded density representative continuous at the target, bandwidths b_n → 0 and n b_n → ∞, and inherited AC/DC. The no-alias corollary additionally requires that representative to agree with the alias sum at the target.

load_bearing.statement: For a real square-integrable lattice field with constant mean and lag-dependent covariance, assuming AC and DC, there is a unique finite positive Radon torus spectral measure F with c(h)=∫exp(i h·θ) F(dθ). For every n≥1 and torus frequency λ, E[I_n(λ)]=∫Φ_n(λ−θ) F(dθ), where Φ_n is nonnegative and has angular integral one.

Assume AC and DC. For a real wide-stationary field whose covariance has a specified nonnegative integrable Borel density f, sampling at spacing δ>0 gives the torus spectral density g_δ(θ)=δ^(-d)∑_k f((θ+2πk)/δ). This sum is finite almost everywhere, has integral ∫f=C(0), and yields both stated periodic-kernel periodogram expectation identities.

Assume AC and DC. If the lattice spectral measure has a specified bounded density representative continuous at λ₀, and the defined kernel and bandwidths satisfy b_n→0 and n b_n→∞, the smoothing denominator is eventually positive and both E[I_n(λ₀)] and E[the smoothed estimator at λ₀] converge to f(λ₀).
The map Ψ:T^d→the Pontryagin dual of discrete Z^d, defined by Ψ(z)(k)=∏_r z_r^(k_r), is a topological group isomorphism for the product and compact-open topologies.
For a positive lag pair count N_n(h), the raw-product covariance estimator is N_n(h)^(-1)∑_{j∈P_n(h)}Y_jY_{j+h}−bar(Y)_n², and the empirical semivariogram is (2N_n(h))^(-1)∑_{j∈P_n(h)}(Y_{j+h}−Y_j)².

Assume Countable Choice. For a jointly measurable real field on R^d with constant mean μ, finite second moments, stationary covariance C∈L¹(R^d), and a Van Hove sequence, every spatial window average is well-defined, has expectation μ, and converges to μ in L².

seams_checked.note: Checked the prerequisite page and its field definition against the consumer definitions, hypotheses, and proofs. Spatial integrals explicitly require joint measurability; wide stationarity preserves constant means and lag covariance, with reverse lags justified by real covariance symmetry. The semivariogram uses raw increment second moments without imposing zero mean increments. The alias lemma explicitly assumes a continuous-space density rather than deriving one from a spectral measure. No converse beyond the supplier statements is used.
